title: Contracts folder: equipment vendor and SaaS terms

title: Intake interview: owner
source_system: Interview (Owner and General Manager)

title: Intake interview: Office Manager
source_system: Interview (Office Manager)
what_it_shows: The Office Manager creates accounting and payroll accounts and asks the MSP for suite accounts; leavers lose suite and payroll access on their last day; there is no leaver checklist; shared passwords and the smokehouse PIN were not changed after the March 2026 departure; payroll exports are saved to the office desktop; in 2025 an email asked her to change a meat supplier's bank details and she called the supplier and stopped it, and staff were not told; she uses public chatbots to draft customer emails and price letters; staff have had no security training

title: Intake interview: Production Supervisor and Maintenance and Sanitation Technician
source_system: Interview (Production Supervisor; Maintenance and Sanitation Technician)
what_it_shows: Cook cycles, formulations and label templates are changed by whoever has the PIN or the labeling PC login, with no record and no second check; the Production Supervisor checks the first label of each run; the smokehouse manufacturer and the packaging vendor connect for support when they choose; the AI camera has run beside the first-label check since 2026-06-15 with no written test plan; cold-chain alerts reach the Production Supervisor's phone; the old packaging controller was taken away in June 2026

source_system: Plant, production office, office and network closet (observation)

title: BIA interviews with process owners
source_system: Interviews (owner, Production Supervisor, Maintenance and Sanitation Technician, Office Manager, MSP lead technician)
what_it_shows: Each owner's description of their process, the systems, vendors and people it uses, its manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss they say it can tolerate; staff describe paper CCP forms and a manual temperature log used informally, with nothing written down; only the Production Supervisor knows the smokehouse cycles day to day, with the owner as backup reviewer

title: Risk assessment interviews
source_system: Interviews (owner, Production Supervisor, Maintenance and Sanitation Technician, Office Manager, 2 production workers, MSP lead technician)
what_it_shows: Owners' accounts of past events and near misses; staff describe approving MFA prompts without checking them and calling the Office Manager about most problems; no call-back rule for bank detail changes; the March 2026 leaver still knew the shared passwords and the PIN in July; no standby generator and no written hurricane procedure; spoilage insurance in place; the MSP lead technician states that its platform uses named technician accounts, with no supporting evidence supplied

title: Gap analysis interviews
source_system: Interviews (owner 2026-07-20; Production Supervisor and Maintenance and Sanitation Technician 2026-07-23; Office Manager; 2 production workers; MSP lead technician)
what_it_shows: The owner confirms the product list and that no FDA-regulated product is made; the Production Supervisor describes product holds for equipment breakdowns and no procedure for lost electronic monitoring or a suspected unauthorized change to a cycle, formulation or label; cycle and template changes are not recorded; the 2026 equipment and cycle changes were not treated as reassessment triggers; records are shown to FSIS on the tablets and in the binder; the smokehouse PIN and the labeling PC password have not changed since 2024; the MSP lead technician states that the backup console and firewall logins use a password only and that no restore test has been run; nobody reviews logs

title: Plant walkthrough, 2026-07-22
source_system: Plant, sanitation room, production office and network closet (observation)
what_it_shows: Chemicals stored in a locked cage in the sanitation room; the floor matches the flow charts except for the new packager, label printer-applicator and camera; the labeling PC and floor tablets do not lock; the remote desktop password note at the labeling PC (photographed); the cold-chain gateway on the office network with no cellular backup; the stuffer HMI on the same network; operational sanitation carried out as written

title: SSOP and HACCP record sample, June and July 2026
source_system: Food safety records app (SYS-05); smokehouse cook logs; pre-shipment review entries
what_it_shows: SSOP pre-operational and operational entries present for all 20 sampled production days, under the shared tablet login with typed initials; corrective action entries record disposition and recurrence steps; for 15 sampled lots, times are recorded automatically, manual cook and receiving checks carry typed initials, and the pre-shipment review was done by the Production Supervisor, who made many of the entries; weekly verification and direct observation entries present

title: Security and compliance lead designation letter
source_system: Office files

title: AI-001 pilot results and camera update history, 2026-06-15 to 2026-08-21
source_system: Seeded defect log (Production Supervisor); camera vendor dashboard (SYS-12)
collected_by: Office Manager, with the Production Supervisor
what_it_shows: 148 of 150 seeded label errors detected (both misses were wrong lot codes on a curved jerky pouch); 113 of 120 seeded seal defects detected, 23 of 28 for snack sticks; false reject rate 3.4% overall and 6.1% in the two weeks after the 2026-07-28 film supplier change; model updates pushed by the vendor on 2026-07-09 and 2026-08-04 with no notice; rejects logged in the vendor dashboard only

title: Control assessment: account management test
source_system: Suite, records app, accounting, cold-chain dashboard, labeling PC and smokehouse portal user lists compared with the staff roster; March 2026 leaver record; Office Manager and MSP lead technician interviews
what_it_shows: Account types are not documented; shared accounts are not prohibited in any approved document (POL-02 B.1 was a draft) and five shared logins are in use; the Office Manager manages accounting, records app and dashboard accounts and the MSP manages suite and PC accounts; the records app has one shared floor role; the roster lists the 7 authorized users; the shared labeling PC login is a local administrator; no written approval for new accounts, and the delivery driver was given the shared dashboard login by text message; the March 2026 leaver's suite account was disabled the same day, and the shared passwords and smokehouse PIN he knew were changed on 2026-08-12; a former worker's dashboard login was removed on 2026-08-12; suite sign-in alerts are not read; the Office Manager learns of each termination the same day; unnamed manufacturer technicians use the smokehouse portal with no authorization on file; office users' access matches their duties; accounts have never been reviewed; the one 2025 role change had accounting access added the same day

title: Control assessment: remote access review
source_system: Smokehouse portal settings and July 2026 session log (from the manufacturer); remote desktop tool settings on the labeling PC; MSP agent description; vendor and staff interviews
what_it_shows: No usage restrictions, connection requirements or guidance for any type of remote access; the smokehouse module was always on and the remote desktop tool accepted unattended sessions with a static password; the portal log shows 6 manufacturer sessions in July 2026 that nobody at the plant requested, which the manufacturer described as routine remote diagnostics; both vendor paths were set to supervised, on-request sessions on 2026-08-12; the packaging vendor had not answered the request for its remote access practices by the end of fieldwork

title: Control assessment: identification and authentication review
source_system: Records app user list; labeling PC accounts; smokehouse controller PIN; 15 lots of CCP records
what_it_shows: Floor users share the records app login and the labeling PC login, and the smokehouse uses one operator PIN; CCP entries, label template edits and cycle changes in the 15 lots cannot be tied to a person, as entries carry typed initials only

title: Control assessment: privileged MFA sign-in tests
source_system: Sign-in attempts to the firewall, backup console, records app administrator and smokehouse portal, with the MSP lead technician present
what_it_shows: All 4 privileged logins accepted a password alone; MFA works on the named suite mailboxes and the accounting service

title: Control assessment: training records and staff interviews
source_system: Document request; interviews with 5 of 7 employees
what_it_shows: No security awareness training of any kind exists, and no records were produced; the 2025 invoice fraud attempt was never shared with staff

title: Control assessment: records integrity test
source_system: Records app administrator settings and edit history; cook-log export folder on the labeling PC; controller log settings; a test edit on a copy of a cook-log export
what_it_shows: The shared vendor default administrator can delete records app entries; cook-log exports are editable spreadsheets, and a test edit on a copy left no trace; the controller log can be cleared from its web interface; nobody is alerted when records or logs are changed or deleted

title: Control assessment: inventory review and network scan
source_system: MSP device list (received 2026-08-06); network scan from the office desktop with a slow, safe profile
what_it_shows: The MSP device list has the 3 managed PCs, with no duplicates and no components from other systems; the scan found 17 devices, including the smokehouse controller, the packager PLC, the stuffer HMI, the AI camera and the cold-chain gateway; machine controllers, tablets, phones, the gateway and SaaS services are not on the list; no firmware versions, owners or network connections recorded; the list has never been reviewed or updated

title: Control assessment: contingency plan review
source_system: Document request; draft BIA (P05); Production Supervisor, Office Manager and owner interviews
what_it_shows: No contingency plan exists; essential functions and recovery objectives appear only in the draft BIA; paper fallbacks are described by staff but not written; staff described a manual temperature log, and none had been done in 2026

title: Control assessment: contingency test review
source_system: MSP confirmation of 2026-08-07; MSP lead technician interview
what_it_shows: No contingency plan test or backup restore test has ever been run; the MSP confirmed on 2026-08-07 that no restore test record exists

title: Control assessment: backup review
source_system: Backup job report for July 2026 and retention settings (received 2026-08-07); backup vendor documentation; machine setting copies requested
what_it_shows: Nightly backups of the office desktop, the labeling PC and the productivity suite completed on 30 of 31 nights in July 2026; smokehouse cycles, stuffer HMI settings and packager recipes are not backed up; HACCP plans, SSOPs and the draft SSP sit in the suite, which is backed up nightly; the backup vendor encrypts stored copies; backups are not immutable and one MSP administrator login without MFA can change or delete them; 30 days of versions; never restore-tested

title: Control assessment: external services review
source_system: Contracts folder (MSP, smokehouse manufacturer, packaging vendor, records app, cold-chain service, AI camera, payroll, suite); MSP technician list and MFA statement (received 2026-08-12); Office Manager interview
what_it_shows: No vendor contract contains security requirements; no privacy requirements for the payroll service or the suite beyond standard terms; no controls required of vendors that reach plant machines; no defined oversight of the MSP or equipment vendors; the MSP scope document defines MSP and customer duties, including the exclusion of plant equipment; no SOC 2 report had been reviewed by the end of fieldwork; the MSP technician list and its MFA statement arrived on 2026-08-12, the last day of fieldwork

title: Control assessment: boundary protection test
source_system: Firewall rule export and log settings (received 2026-08-06); reachability tests from the office desktop; guest Wi-Fi test; smokehouse controller web interface sign-in
what_it_shows: The firewall keeps 7 days of logs and nobody reviews them; unsolicited inbound traffic is blocked and any outbound connection is allowed, including vendor remote tools; no internal interfaces exist; from the office desktop the assessor reached the smokehouse controller web interface, the packager HMI and the AI camera; the controller web interface accepted the manufacturer default administrator password, which was changed the same day, and the July cook logs checked against the handheld readings showed no unexplained changes; guest Wi-Fi is separated from the staff network; one internet connection through the managed firewall; the card terminal uses the provider's cellular link

title: Control assessment: malicious code protection test
source_system: Antivirus console export (received 2026-08-06); harmless industry-standard test file on the labeling PC; after-hours test alert at 18:30
what_it_shows: Antivirus on all 3 managed PCs and email filtering in the suite; the stuffer HMI cannot run antivirus; the test file was quarantined within seconds; signatures update automatically; weekly full scans, real-time scanning and quarantine configured; the 18:30 test alert was seen at 08:10 the next day, as the MSP watches alerts in business hours only; the MSP reviewed and released two false positives in July 2026
